title: Protein synthesis
examples: What is the role of transfer RNA in protein synthesis?
How does the sequence of codons determine the amino acid chain?
Can you explain the difference between transcription and translation?

explain.say: Today we will learn about protein synthesis in cells. This process builds proteins using genetic instructions.
First is transcription. This copies a segment of DNA into messenger RNA. This happens in the nucleus of the cell.
Next is translation. The ribosome reads the mRNA sequence to build a polypeptide chain. This occurs in the cytoplasm.
The genetic code uses codons. A codon is a sequence of three bases on the mRNA. Each codon specifies one amino acid.

draw.text: Codon: Three bases = One amino acid

explain.say: In real life, when your body needs to make an enzyme, the DNA instructions are first copied to mRNA, and then the mRNA guides the building of the enzyme.
A common mistake is thinking that DNA directly builds the protein. Remember, mRNA acts as the temporary messenger molecule first.

faq.q: What is the difference between DNA and RNA?
faq.a: DNA is a double helix found in the nucleus, while RNA is usually single-stranded and functions as a messenger. You might also ask what the structural difference is, or where the genetic material is stored.
asks: What is the difference between DNA and RNA?
Where is the genetic code kept?
Is RNA the same as mRNA?

faq.q: Does every gene get transcribed at the same time?
faq.a: No, only the genes needed at that specific time and place are transcribed. This allows cells to be very specialized. You could also ask how gene expression is controlled, or which genes are active.
asks: Do all genes in the cell work all the time?

faq.q: What is the role of tRNA in translation?
faq.a: Transfer RNA carries specific amino acids to the ribosome, matching them to the codons on the mRNA. It acts like a physical adaptor molecule. Another way to ask is what reads the amino acid onto the chain, or what brings the amino acid to the ribosome.
asks: What brings the amino acid to the ribosome?
What is the adaptor molecule in translation?
How does tRNA know which amino acid to carry?

faq.a: A codon is simply a sequence of three adjacent bases on the mRNA strand. This three-base unit specifies one particular amino acid. You might also ask what three bases code for one amino acid, or what the reading unit is.
asks: What is the reading unit of the genetic code?
How many bases make up one codon?

faq.q: Does the process happen in the nucleus or the cytoplasm?
faq.a: Transcription happens inside the nucleus, where the DNA is located. Translation then moves to the ribosomes in the cytoplasm. You could ask where the two processes occur, or which organelle is involved in building protein.
asks: Does transcription happen outside the nucleus?
What is the location for protein synthesis?

facts: Transcription copies DNA information into mRNA in the nucleus.
Translation uses ribosomes to read mRNA codons and build proteins.
Each codon specifies one amino acid according to the genetic code.
The process requires energy, usually in the form of ATP.

quiz.say: If the mRNA codon sequence is AUG, which amino acid is coded for?
quiz.why: AUG is the universal start codon that codes for the amino acid Methionine, initiating protein synthesis.

wrong.1: Alanine is coded by different codons, so this is incorrect.
wrong.2: Water is a molecule, not an amino acid specified by a codon.
wrong.3: DNA is the template, not the amino acid product.

quiz.say: What molecule carries the amino acid to the ribosome during translation?
quiz.why: Transfer RNA (tRNA) is specifically responsible for physically bringing the correct amino acid to the ribosome based on the mRNA codon.

wrong.0: rRNA is a structural component of the ribosome, not the carrier.
wrong.1: DNA is the master template, not involved in the direct transfer step.
wrong.3: mRNA only carries the code, not the amino acid itself.

quiz.say: If the DNA template strand reads TAC, what will the complementary mRNA codon be?
quiz.why: During transcription, the base pairing rules dictate that T in DNA pairs with A in RNA, A pairs with U, and C pairs with G, resulting in AUG.

wrong.1: This incorrectly pairs T with U and C with C.
wrong.2: This incorrectly transcribes the T base.
wrong.3: The mRNA must use Uracil instead of Thymine.
